doc.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: What does it mean to swing
summary: He says swing is about time and cannot explain it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Is it possible for you to describe, if someone knew nothing about swing music—
I know what you’re going to ask me.
Could you tell them? What’s it mean to swing?

That’s always been a hard thing to answer. I’ll tell you. It has a lot to do with timing, with time. See because the most important ingredient that anybody can have as a musician first is time. And you can have all the technique in the world but if you don’t have that time, which is, then forget it, it won’t swing. So I don’t know, it’s a hard question to answer. Swing. It’s one of the roughest questions.
It is. And I rarely get an answer so don’t feel bad.
I can swing like crazy, but I can’t explain it.
You have to listen to it.
And I can go through a million changes, Latin chords and everything, but I can’t name them for you.
Well you certainly have it innate in you, right inside.
Swing. You threw me now. That’s such a hard one to answer.
